title: open()
summary: Open a file and return a file object. Always use it with `with`.
description: Text mode decodes bytes using `encoding`; binary mode ('b') does not. Always pass `encoding='utf-8'` explicitly — the default depends on the platform locale, so the same code can behave differently in a container.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: r read, w truncate-write, a append, x exclusive create, b binary.

parameters.name: newline
parameters.description: Pass '' when reading or writing CSV.

raises.when: Mode 'r' and the file does not exist.
The process may not access the path.
Mode 'x' and the file already exists.

examples.title: Read safely
examples.code: with open('data.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n    text = f.read()

examples.title: Stream a large file
examples.code: with open('huge.log', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n    for line in f:\n        process(line)

real_world_usage: `pathlib.Path.read_text()` / `write_text()` are cleaner for whole small files. Use open() when you need to stream, append, or work in binary.

common_mistakes.fix: An exception then leaks the handle and can lose buffered writes.

common_mistakes.mistake: Opening with 'w' to inspect a file
common_mistakes.fix: 'w' truncates on open, before you write anything. Use 'r'.
Iterate the handle to stream it line by line.

performance_notes: Buffered by default. Reading line by line is constant memory; `read()` is O(file size) in RAM.
security_notes: Never open a path built from unvalidated user input — `../` escapes any prefix. Resolve the path and verify it is inside the intended directory with `Path.is_relative_to`.
